body:
**Price check**
- Google Finance: ₹726.25 at 19 Nov, 3:30 pm IST (+0.28%).
- Screener price chart: ₹723.70 close on 19 Nov.
- **Discrepancy:** the screener headline box showed ₹736 (₹735.60 in the screen table). That is about 1.3% above the other two, so I used **about ₹725**.
- Earlier dated datapoints: Upstox ₹749 (4 Nov); Kotak ₹673 (23 Oct). The 52-week range is about ₹400–916 (Upstox).
- Recomputed: TTM EPS ₹43.30 (7.38 + 11.33 + 12.54 + 12.05), giving a **P/E of 16.7**. About 4.51 cr shares gives a **market cap of about ₹3,270 cr**. Company-reported **net cash is ₹172 cr**.

**Annual figures (₹ cr)**
| FY | Sales | OPM | PAT | ROCE | Borrowings | CFO |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| FY22 | 1,227 | 22% | 169 | 30% | 158 | 85 |
| FY23 | 1,366 | 22% | 205 | 32% | 61 | 253 |
| FY24 | 1,140 | 18% | 125 | 18% | 103 | 200 |
| FY25 | 964 | 15% | 88 | 12% | 120 | 182 |
| FY26 | 1,170 | 21% | 158 | 22% | 155 | 174 |
| TTM | 1,346 | 22% | 196 | – | 162 (Sep-26) | – |

Over five years, CFO totals ₹894 cr against PAT of ₹745 cr, about 1.2x, which is good cash conversion.

**Quarterly figures (₹ cr)**
| Quarter | Dec-24 | Mar-25 | Jun-25 | Sep-25 | Dec-25 | Mar-26 | Jun-26 | Sep-26 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Sales | 208 | 253 | 274 | 277 | 281 | 339 | 347 | 379 |
| YoY | −20% | −13% | +5% | +15% | +35% | +34% | +27% | +37% |
| OPM | 15% | 14% | 19% | 21% | 20% | 24% | 24% | 22% |
| PAT | 19 | 23 | 34 | 39 | 33 | 51 | 57 | 54 |

There are no loss quarters. OPM has stayed at 19% or higher for six straight quarters. Q2 dipped sequentially (24% → 22%). Management's through-cycle target is above 20%.

**Shareholding**
| Holder | Dec-24 | Sep-26 | Direction |
|---|---|---|---|
| Promoter | 65.66% | 65.85% | Flat |
| FII | 1.81% | 4.43% | **Rising every quarter since Jun-25** |
| DII | 7.84% | 4.09% | Falling |

Shareholder count fell from 84.7k to 63.5k, so retail is leaving and FIIs are accumulating. Promoter pledge is nil, based on the FY26 no-encumbrance declaration and aggregator data, not the BSE filing itself.

**What drives the story**
- This is a cyclical recovery that also has a real mix shift; it is *not* a brand-new step-change. OPM peaked at 22% in FY22–23, fell to 15% in FY25 during the US/EU ag-equipment downturn, and is now back at 22–24% *while the farm segment is still weak*.
- The cause is named: **construction-equipment sales grew 49% YoY in Q2 FY27**, driven by North American data-centre, power and AI-infrastructure builds. Construction is now 45.8% of finished-goods sales, up from 36.9% in FY25.
- Further drivers: the India aftermarket is 16.5% of revenue, ₹225 cr of new business awards are ramping (3-point linkage systems and precision machine parts), and FY27 revenue guidance is about +24%.
- The rupee matters here: revenue is overwhelmingly USD/EUR through its US and EU warehousing subsidiaries, while costs are Indian. Global OEMs are shifting sourcing away from China (China+1).

body: **Summary:** Regulated utilities (NTPC thermal, Power Grid transmission) earn a CERC-set ~15.5% post-tax RoE on regulated equity, so earnings grow with capitalised assets. Renewable IPPs sign 25-year PPAs at fixed tariffs, so returns depend on capex per MW, capacity utilisation factor (CUF), financing cost and the counterparty (SECI or a state discom). Merchant power and exchanges (IEX) depend on spot prices and volumes. Key metrics: regulated equity growth, capacity commissioned against target, PLF/CUF, PPA tariff against capex (equity IRR), net debt/EBITDA, receivables days from discoms, and merchant exposure. Cycle drivers: power demand growth (peak 270.8 GW in May 2026), coal supply and imported coal prices, interest rates, module and battery prices (the China price collapse 2023–25), ALMM and duty policy, discom finances (LPS rules 2022), and transmission and curtailment bottlenecks. Lead indicators: CEA daily and monthly generation reports, Grid-India peak demand, IEX daily prices, MNRE capacity additions, PFC discom ratings, Coal India offtake. Winners kept a regulated or contracted balance sheet with cheap financing, or picked merchant exposure at the right time (JSW Energy, Tata Power 2022–24). Losers were the 2010–13 thermal IPPs with merchant or untied PPAs and imported coal (Lanco, GVK, RPower) and governance blow-ups (Gensol 2025). Valuation: regulated utilities at 1.2–2.5x P/B (re-rated in 2023–24), renewables at 15–25x EV/EBITDA. Nov 2026: Q2 FY27 coal PLF was 68%, ~7 GW of RE was added in the quarter, and ICRA expects FY27 additions of ~50 GW. Traps: capacity announcements over commissioning, and discom receivables. Sources: [1](https://energyandcleanair.org/quarterly-energy-snapshot-for-india-q2-2026-27/) · [2](https://www.icra.in/Research/ViewResearchReport/power-sector/7091) · [3](https://www.downtoearth.org.in/amp/story/energy/power-demand-tracker-india-meets-all-time-high-power-demand-of-2708-gw-renewable-energy-share-34) Links: about `case_study:gensol-2025`

**Rules** were written to `research_notes/Deep dives/UTKARSHBNK_selection/prereg_selection.md` at **2026-11-24 16:33 IST, before the frame was
built** (sha256 of the rule text recorded in the file). Seen before writing: universe.csv header; the live-dd4 prereg/selection lists (healthcare
+ IT names, no financials, no mcaps); `industry_map.csv` checked and **absent**, so lenders were hand-classified.
- Close: the 24-Nov bhavcopy returned HTTP 404 at 16:33 IST → 23-Nov-2026 close (rule 1). Mcap = universe shares × close.
- Frame: 1,547 symbols, all priced; **809** in ₹1,000–20,000 cr; 482 with no index industry.
- Sector lists (written into the prereg **before the shuffle**): IT 36 (index 18 + hand 18, same judgments as dd4); lenders 34 (17 from index
  "Financial Services" + 17 hand-classified from unindexed names). Excluded as non-lenders or unsure: holdcos (BAJAJHLDNG, EDELWEISS, JMFINANCIL,
  IFCI, BFINVEST…), brokers, RTAs, AMC, exchange, ratings, primary dealer. **Eligible = 70.**
- Draw: `random.Random(20261202).shuffle` of the sorted list. First 15: KPITTECH, **UTKARSHBNK**, CYIENT, SATIN, TANLA, MPSLTD, UJJIVANSFB, PSB,
  INTELLECT, RAMCOSYS, REPCOHOME, ESAFSFB, SAMMAANCAP, ONEPOINT, PAISALO.

| # | Symbol | Mcap ₹ cr | Result | Reason |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | KPITTECH | 14,317 | **skip (d)** | Passed a–c (only subsidiaries merged into it; the Nov-2023 "change in auditors" is KPIT UK's; pledge flags false). **PEAD Q2 FY27 SUE −0.81 → quintile 1, event 28-Oct-2026, inside the 63-trading-day window.** |
| 2 | **UTKARSHBNK** | 2,084 | **SUBJECT** | a: the pending scheme merges the promoter holdco Utkarsh CoreInvest (UCL) **into** the bank — the listed bank survives. b: SEBI settlement Apr-2024 (₹1.24 cr, LODR) is not a fraud finding; FY26 audit unmodified; no RBI restriction. c: pledge flags false. d: SUE +1.53 → Q5. e: lender form — CRAR 17.0% ≥ 15%, ratings A- (investment grade). |

Notes: the defensive layer again removed the first name (as in dd3/dd4). The subject entered via the **hand-classified** lender list (no index
industry), as INDRAMEDCO did — the missing industry map keeps mattering. PEAD quintiles for the first 15 were printed together before the walk;
the walk order was not changed.
